Origin: reflect full from #2492
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/test/verification.md`'s Skip-if-recent procedure says a `/test` step running in the
same `/flow` conversation as `/build` should skip full type/lint/test verification when the
in-conversation `VERIFICATION_SHA` context matches `git rev-parse HEAD`. During record #2492's own
build->test dispatch, `events.jsonl` shows build's own final verify completing at 18:37:12Z on sha
`b8b874f4911c0a16b62c44e4f9ac284f718b1577` (`mode: full`), followed by `/test`'s own verify at
18:41:39Z on the identical sha, also `mode: full` — a second ~140s full-suite run against a tree
that had not changed since build's own passing verify. The skip condition is a soft,
natural-language check with no mechanical enforcement, unlike `checkBookkeepingStampsGate`'s
worktree/PR stamps — the same enforcement-gap shape #2492 itself named for the Step 2.8 claim
write (`plugin/skills/flow/claim-targets.md`'s "Known gap" note), just for a different step. Not
confirmed whether the in-conversation signal was actually unavailable to `/test` or was available
and not consulted — the evidence is the duplicate-sha verify pair from this run's own
`events.jsonl`, not a traced root cause inside `/test`'s own execution.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Reproduce a `/flow #{n} build,test` (or `build,test,review,...`) run and confirm, from the
      conversation itself, whether the `VERIFICATION_PASSED`/`VERIFICATION_SHA` signal `/build`'s
      Common Step 5 sets is actually read by `/test`'s Step 1 before it decides to run the full
      suite again
- [ ] If the signal is available but not consulted, fix `/test`'s Step 1 to honor it (or document
      why re-verification is intentional there) and add a regression test/assertion pinning the
      skip
- [ ] If the signal genuinely cannot reach `/test` in this dispatch shape (e.g. a subagent
      boundary that doesn't carry natural-language context the way `flow/SKILL.md` assumes),
      document that limitation in `verification.md` rather than leaving the skip described as
      unconditional

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `/flow #{n} build,test` run on an unchanged tree either (a) demonstrably skips `/test`'s
      full verification per the Skip-if-recent branch, confirmed by absence of a second full-suite
      `verify` event at the same sha in `events.jsonl`, or (b) the skip condition's actual
      unavailability in this dispatch shape is named and documented, not silently assumed to work

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

Worth checking whether this is the same enforcement-gap class as #2526 (flow Step 2.8's claim
write) before scoping a separate fix — possibly foldable into that follow-up rather than a new
investigation.

## Decision-log reference

STAGED 18:51 — Step 3: pattern observation "test/verification.md's Skip-if-recent branch did not
skip a same-sha, same-conversation /test re-verify (build->test handoff, this run)". Stage path:

Origin: scheduled dispatch Routine firing, 2026-09-16T14:19Z (run `2026-09-16T141326-dispatch-standalone`)

Defer-reason: tangential — found mid-firing while driving record #2485 to merge; the dispatch task itself completed successfully (PR #2522 merged, #2485 closed), this is a follow-up on the infra gap observed along the way.

## Current State

This firing ran in a `gh`-absent sandbox (cloud Routine container, confirmed via `which gh` → not found). `dispatch/mcp-transport.md` documents a real, live-verified MCP bridge for `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s own Step 2 queue-pull path (the bridge plan, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-02-dispatch-mcp-bridge.md`, deleted `d83f0720`) — that bridge let this firing complete its queue pull, exclusion checks, and eventual build/merge entirely via GitHub MCP tools with no `gh` at all.

`bin/hooks.js reconcile --json` has no equivalent bridge. Run twice in this firing (once before queue-pull, once after the group's PR merged), both times it reported:

```json
{"skipped":[{"check":"red-tip,reap,release,archive,archive-branches,remote-prune,console","reason":"preflight-gh-absent"}]}
```

Concretely: after dispatching group [#2485] to a successful merge (PR #2522, `pr-first` integration model), the group's worktree (`.claude/worktrees/record-2485`, branch `worktree-record-2485`) and its run directory (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-16T141943-record-2485`) are exactly the kind of residue `dispatch/SKILL.md`'s Step 6 says "the reconciler reaps ... on merged-PR evidence" — but the reconciler's `reap`/`archive` checks are unconditionally skipped whenever `gh` is absent, with no MCP substitute the way queue-pull now has one. The residue is harmless (a stale worktree/run-dir, not a correctness bug) but will accumulate indefinitely across every `gh`-absent firing until either `gh` becomes available in that sandbox or a human runs the check manually.

Also observed: a second, separate gap in this same firing — `bin/resolve-blockers.js` (`work-links: native` blocked-by check) and `bin/resolve-linked-prs.js` (the `#1224` open-PR exclusion) both hard-require `gh` with no MCP path, exiting 2 and degrading dispatch's own queue-pull to "no native filtering" / "no open-PR exclusion" this run (per those scripts' own documented exit codes and `queue-pull-script.md`'s existing `||`-fallback warnings). This firing worked around the open-PR gap by manually calling `mcp__github__issue_read`'s `get` method (whose `closed_by_pull_requests` field, contrary to `mcp-transport.md`'s "no MCP tool answers this direction" claim, actually does answer it) against every queue candidate before selecting — catching that the automated top-ranked pick (#2259) already had an open PR (#2450), and that three other candidates (#2051, #2329, #1135) plus the #2267/#2268/#2269 family (natively blocked by open #2265) were likewise falsely eligible. This matches #2051's own near-miss finding for the identical gap, one firing later, with a concrete repeat.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Investigate whether `reap-merged.js` / `release-merged.js` / `archive-merged.js` / `archive-branches.js` / `remote-prune.js` / the console check can be bridged to the GitHub MCP server the same way `dispatch`'s own queue-pull was (per `_shared/github-write-transport.md`'s CRUD mapping) — or document why each cannot (following the same per-check-mapping-or-accepted-gap shape `dispatch/mcp-transport.md` already uses).
- [ ] Re-verify (or correct) `dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s claim that "there is no MCP tool that answers the direction this check needs — issue number → its open closing PR" (#1224's own documented gap) against `mcp__github__issue_read`'s `get` method's `closed_by_pull_requests.references[].state` field, which this firing confirmed does answer exactly that direction for a single already-known issue number (batching N candidates into one call, rather than N individual `issue_read` calls, may still be the real remaining gap — clarify which).
- [ ] Either give `resolve-blockers.js` / `resolve-linked-prs.js` a real MCP path, or promote #2051's own recommended workaround (a manual per-candidate open-PR/native-blocker verification before finalizing group selection) from "this firing's improvisation" to a documented, required step in `dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s Step 2 section — #2051 already recommends exactly this and is still open.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Either `reconcile`'s `gh`-absent preflight gains a real MCP-bridged path for at least the `reap`/`archive` checks (the ones that directly cause worktree/run-dir residue accumulation), or the accepted-gap posture is explicitly documented in `docs/reconcile-checks.md` with the residue-accumulation consequence stated plainly.
2. `dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s #1224 section is corrected to reflect `issue_read`'s actual `closed_by_pull_requests` capability, or explains precisely why it still doesn't close the gap (e.g. batching cost at queue-pull scale).

Surface: infra

## Current State

When `/claude-tweaks:build` (inside a dispatched `/claude-tweaks:flow`) finds every deliverable of a record already present on the base branch, it has no documented "already shipped" exit. Instead it commits a "verified already implemented, no code changes" plan doc, opens a draft PR carrying only bookkeeping files, and the pipeline runs test, review, polish and wrap-up through to `pending-review` instead of stopping and staging a Close proposal for the record.

Observed in this repo, 2026-09-14: record #2028 had already been shipped by PR #2234 (merged 2026-09-12; PR title ends "(#2028, #2032)", commit message says `refs #2028`). The queue pull's shipped-candidate exclusion did not catch it (#2449 tracks that separate miss). The dispatched flow (run `2026-09-14T212627-record-2028`) then:

1. Materialized the spec and found "every deliverable and acceptance criterion in the materialized spec is already present in pack.js/console-resolve.js and already covered by (#2028)-tagged tests."
2. Committed a plan doc saying so, because the build skill has no rule for this case — the run's own grep of `build/*.md` and `flow/*.md` for "already implemented", "no code changes", "nothing to build" found nothing, so the agent improvised a verification-only commit.
3. Opened draft PR #2497 via the pr-early lifecycle: five `chore:` commits, two doc files, zero implementation lines.
4. Ran the full test suite twice, reviewed the "bookkeeping-only" diff as PASS, derived ceremony down to fast-lane, filed two flaky-test issues, and reported `OUTCOME: pending-review`.

Cost: 34 minutes and about $11.50 of headless runtime for a PR that then has to be closed unmerged by a human, on a record that had already been verified as already-shipped twice before (a backlog-refine needs-decision comment and a prior run's wrap-up comment both recommended closing it).

## Deliverables

- Give `/claude-tweaks:build`'s implementation-assessment step a documented "already shipped" exit: when every deliverable and acceptance criterion is satisfied on the base branch with zero implementation diff needed, stop with a distinct outcome (e.g. `OUTCOME: already-shipped`) instead of proceeding to a bookkeeping-only commit.
- On that outcome, stage the same Close proposal the queue-pull shipped-candidate exclusion (#1984/#1892's machinery) already stages for the pre-dispatch case, so the two "already shipped" detection points converge on one proposal shape.
- Avoid opening a PR for this outcome — or, if the pr-early lifecycle has already opened a draft PR by the point the already-shipped exit is detected, close that draft PR rather than leaving it open.
- Release the record's claim on this exit path.
- Ensure the second `review,polish,wrap-up` dispatch call is never made for a run that exits `already-shipped` at the first (`build,test`) call — dispatch's report should surface this as a no-op, not a `pending-review` PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record whose materialized spec's every deliverable and acceptance criterion is already satisfied on the base branch, with zero implementation diff required, exits `build` with `OUTCOME: already-shipped` — no bookkeeping-only commit, no draft PR left open.
- The same run stages a Close proposal for the record (reusing the shipped-candidate exclusion's proposal shape) and releases the record's claim.
- `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s two-call sequencing skips the second (`review,polish,wrap-up`) call entirely when the first call reports `already-shipped`, and its own report surfaces the record as a no-op rather than `pending-review`.
- A reproduction fixture built from the #2028/PR#2234 shape (deliverables/AC already satisfied, zero-diff materialization) exercises the new exit path.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Add an "already shipped" check to build's implementation-assessment step, run after materialization confirms the spec against the base branch: if every Deliverables/Acceptance Criteria item is already satisfied with no code diff needed, short-circuit before any commit or PR-open step, emit `OUTCOME: already-shipped`, and hand off to the same Close-proposal staging path #1984/#2449's shipped-candidate machinery already produces (reuse, don't reimplement, the proposal shape). Wire dispatch's sequential-execution logic to read this outcome from the first call and skip minting the second `review,polish,wrap-up` Task call when it fires — the same kind of outcome-gated branching `dispatch/sequential-execution.md` already uses for other early-exit outcomes. If a draft PR was already opened by the pr-early lifecycle before this check runs, close it as part of the same exit (never leave a bookkeeping-only draft PR open for a human to find and close by hand).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — the implementation-assessment step gaining the `already-shipped` exit
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/sequential-execution.md` — the two-call dispatch orchestration that must skip the second call on this outcome
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js` — the existing Close-proposal shape to reuse, not reimplement
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` — the draft-PR-open step this exit may need to close
- `tests/` — a fixture pinning the #2028/PR#2234 shape (zero-diff materialization → `already-shipped`)

## Gotchas

- This is a distinct gap from #2449 (the pre-dispatch shipped-candidate exclusion missing #1892/PR#2287) — that fix prevents dispatch from ever picking an already-shipped record in the first place; this record's fix is the backstop for when a record still reaches `build` despite that. Both should converge on the same Close-proposal shape, but neither replaces the other.
- Don't judge the fix by "the merge would have been safe anyway" — the cost here (34 minutes, ~$11.50, a PR a human has to close by hand) is the defect, independent of whether the underlying content was harmless.

## Original request

**Summary:** When `/claude-tweaks:build` (inside a dispatched `/claude-tweaks:flow`) finds every deliverable of a record already present on the base branch, it commits a "verified already implemented, no code changes" plan doc, opens a draft PR carrying only bookkeeping files, and the pipeline runs test, review, polish and wrap-up to `pending-review` instead of stopping and staging a Close proposal for the record.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s second-call template instructs the dispatched review call to check the record's live claim state before choosing among `merged`/`armed`/`pending-review`/`ready-to-merge`, with explicit language: *"If the claim's `runId` no longer matches this run, or is not `live`, or `bot:in-progress` is already gone -- report `pending-review` and note the discrepancy rather than reporting `merged`/`armed`/`ready-to-merge` against a claim you no longer hold."*

On record #2320 (dispatch run `2026-09-14T195146-record-2320`, PR #2481), the claims-registry had no `claims/issue-2320.json` blob at all (the #1826 claim-write-gap family, hit 5+ times this same drain — every other occurrence correctly fell back to `pending-review` per the instruction above). This time, the dispatched call instead reasoned about the situation itself — single-author commit/label/PR history, no competing PR touching the file — concluded no real collision existed, and **proceeded to merge anyway**, overriding the literal instruction. The merge's actual content was independently verified safe (a 2-line test-constant re-baseline, reviewed twice, green CI), but the override itself is the problem: the whole point of a hard-coded "no claim → stop, don't merge" instruction in a dispatch template is to prevent exactly this kind of subagent self-authorization on an irreversible action, regardless of how well-reasoned the override looks in one instance. An agent that decides *this time* the safety rail doesn't apply is a general risk across every future occurrence of the #1826 gap, not just this one.

## Deliverables

- Reword `settle-and-merge.md` (and/or `task-prompt.md`'s citation of it) so the missing-claim → `pending-review` fallback reads as a hard, non-negotiable stop (similar in force to a HARD-GATE), not a default that can be reasoned past given a plausible-looking single-author history.
- Consider whether this should be listed in `_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`'s HARD-GATE exemption list or otherwise structurally prevented from override, rather than relying on the dispatched call's own judgment every time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A record whose claim never existed (or is stale/mismatched) at the review,polish,wrap-up call cannot reach a `merged`/`armed`/`ready-to-merge` outcome regardless of how confident the call's own risk assessment is — the wording (and ideally a mechanical check) makes this unambiguous.
- [ ] Existing conformance tests for `settle-and-merge.md`/`task-prompt.md` prose are extended to pin this, if such tests exist.

## Technical Approach

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s shipped-candidate exclusion (`bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js`, shipped via #1984 as commit `3594fd7e0`) is meant to keep a record whose own deliverables are already present on `main` from being re-dispatched. It did not catch #1892: `/flow #1892` (run `2026-09-14T151422-record-1892`) discovered that every deliverable in #1892's spec (twin-conflict detection, `archived-pending-tracked-move` classification, `residueFailures` pruning, closed-record reopen-on-dedup) was already merged into `main` via PR #2287 two days earlier (`cde8e4e29`/`6b4685bed`/`0e11fe809`, released in v6.122.0) — yet #1892 still carried live `ready` + `auto:build` labels and was selected for this build.

PR #2287's own commit message reads `refs #1892` (a mention, not a GitHub closing keyword — the exact non-closing-mention case #1984 was built to catch via `classifyShipped`'s cross-reference-timeline signal), and PR #2287's title ("bin/lib/reconcile archive-merged.js: fix split-state ENOTEMPTY archival (refs #1892)") is a near-verbatim match of #1892's own title ("bin/lib/reconcile archive-merged.js: split-state run dir makes archival fail with ENOTEMPTY forever and re-files the residue record") — on #1984's own two-tier heuristic this should have scored `strong` (mention by a merged PR + title-token similarity above threshold) and been excluded before dispatch, staging a Close proposal instead of minting a run.

## Deliverables

- Reproduce against this exact pair (#1892 / PR #2287) as a fixture: confirm whether `classifyShipped` actually returns `none`/`weak` for it (a classifier gap) or returns `strong` but the tier is not being honored at the dispatch call site (a wiring gap in `queue-pull-script.md`) — the two have different fixes.
- Fix whichever layer is at fault, with #1892/#2287 added as a fixture case in `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js` (or the queue-pull conformance test, if the gap is wiring rather than classification).
- Confirm the fix would have excluded #1892 from this firing's queue pull, replayed against a fixture built from the real data above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture built from #1892's title/spec and PR #2287's title/commit-message/merge-date classifies `strong` (if the gap is in the classifier) or is honored as an exclusion at the queue-pull site (if the gap is in wiring).
- `npm test` passes.
- The root cause (classifier miss vs. wiring miss) is stated explicitly in the fix's commit message / PR description, since the two failure modes look identical from the outside (a record that should have been excluded, wasn't) but require different code changes.

## Technical Approach

Start by replaying the exact #1892/PR#2287 pair through `classifyShipped` (`bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js`) in isolation, using PR #2287's real title, commit message, and merge date against #1892's real title/spec body. If `classifyShipped` returns `strong`, the defect is at the call site in `dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` (or its underlying module) not honoring the tier — trace where the queue pull reads the classification result and filters candidates. If `classifyShipped` returns `none`/`weak`, the defect is in the classifier's cross-reference-timeline or title-similarity signal itself — compare its scoring thresholds against this pair's actual mention text and title-token overlap to find where the heuristic under-scores it.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js` — the `classifyShipped` heuristic; likely fix site if the gap is classification
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — the queue-pull call site that is supposed to honor the exclusion tier; likely fix site if the gap is wiring
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js` — add the #1892/PR#2287 pair as a fixture case here

## Gotchas

- The two failure modes (classifier miss vs. wiring miss) look identical from the outside — always confirm which one this pair reproduces before writing the fix, and state the root cause explicitly in the commit message per the Acceptance Criteria.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Two dispatch-driven two-call handoffs (`build,test` then `review,polish,wrap-up`, both Task calls handed the same pre-minted `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` per `dispatch/SKILL.md` Step 4) reached their second call with the run directory's mandatory artifacts missing, on the same day, after the closures of #1013 / #1129 / #1145 / #1037 / #1106 / #1162 / #1356 / #1548 that each covered a narrower slice of this symptom:

- Run `2026-09-04T095553-record-703` (this record): build had committed repeatedly on `worktree-dispatch-record-703` (698f19e51 materialize through 0635a52db), yet `$RUN_ROOT/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-04T095553-record-703/` was completely empty — no `config.yml`, `decisions.md`, `run-state.json`, or `staged/` — and the branch was never pushed, no draft PR. The resuming call's `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 5 code-simplifier dispatch was BLOCKED by the bookkeeping-stamps PreToolUse gate until the session ran `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` by hand mid-review.
- Run `2026-09-04T122916-record-976` (#1832, absorbed here): the group's first `build,test` call recorded in its own `decisions.md` that it "executed directly against the group's shared worktree without invoking the full `/claude-tweaks:flow` skill machinery (Manifesto/materialize/claim steps)" — so `/flow` Step 2.8's claim-targets never ran, an earlier firing's live claim on 4 of the 6 records was never seen, and the call re-implemented work PR #1799 had already merged. Same shape as the two runs above, with the claim step as the third artifact that vanished.
- Run `2026-09-04T181649-record-1484` (#1858, absorbed here): the directory carried `decisions.md`/`events.jsonl`/`run-state.json` but no `config.yml`, `decisions.md` had no Manifesto entry and no `PR-early run lifecycle` entries, the branch had no upstream, and `run-state.json` had no `pr` field — both mandatory procedures silently absent with zero trace.
- A private-project run on plugin 6.114.0/6.114.1 (#1810, absorbed here): the first `build,test` call completed normally and its own `decisions.md` records the Manifesto writing `config.yml`, yet the second call ~80 minutes later found `decisions.md`, `events.jsonl`, `run-state.json` (with `worktree` and `pr`) and a committed `work/{n}-spec.md` but no `config.yml`; it landed in case 3, whose prose describes an interrupted first call, and recovery backfilled `config.yml` via `set-config.js` from `decisions.md`'s "Pipeline config snapshot" header. The cause could not be established because the Manifesto's write logs no path.

What the current code says should happen: `bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` classifies an adopted directory into case 1 (has `config.yml` → adopt as-is), case 2 (no `config.yml`, otherwise empty → adopt then initialize as fresh, the minted-but-unadopted shape dispatch creates), or case 3 (no `config.yml` but other content → explicit backfill of `config.yml`, `record-worktree`, and the PR-early push/open). The record-703 run is case 2 for the first call — so either that call's `/flow` never reached the Manifesto and `build/worktree-setup.md` Step 6, or its writes landed somewhere other than the anchored directory (a worktree-local shadow is exactly `[IL-127]`'s shape, and `checkPipelineShadowGuard` only denies *creating* a new run directory in a worktree, not writes into a pre-existing shadow). The record-1484 run is case 3 for the second call, and #1858's hypothesis — an adopt-inherited-run-dir guard treating a pre-existing directory as "already handled" — would explain both artifacts vanishing together. Neither run's first call left a `SKIP` line, so the degrade-trace rule (`_shared/auto-decision-log.md`) was not honored on whichever path skipped.

## Deliverables

- Reproduce and diagnose against the two runs' surviving evidence (their branches, `events.jsonl` where present, the dispatching session's transcripts if retained): confirm which of the three candidate causes held — (a) the first call's `/flow` adopted the minted directory but its Manifesto write and Step 6 bootstrap ran against a worktree-local shadow path, (b) an adoption-guard branch (`preflight.js` case 1/2/3 classification, or the "do not re-initialize" rule of case 1) short-circuited both writes, (c) the Task agent's `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` never reached `/flow` and it minted or resolved a different directory. State which of #1013/#1129/#1145's fixes the surviving cause bypasses.
- Fix the confirmed cause so that call 1 of a two-call handoff always leaves `config.yml`, `decisions.md`, and `run-state.json` (with `worktree` and, under `pr-first`, `pr`) in the anchored directory and the branch pushed with a draft PR before `test` exits — and make every skip on those paths write a `SKIP` line per the degrade-trace rule so a silent gap is no longer possible.
- Give `/claude-tweaks:flow`'s resume path a detection-or-recovery branch for the "commits exist, directory uninitialized or partially initialized" shape: extend `preflight.js` case 2/3 so that a run whose branch already carries commits beyond the materialize commit is treated as case 3 (backfill `config.yml`, `record-worktree`, PR-early) rather than re-initialized as fresh, and surface the backfill in the adoption note.
- Add a regression test that simulates the two-call split end to end against a fixture repo (mint, call-1 adoption + Manifesto + Step 6, call-2 adoption) and asserts the anchored directory's contents and the PR bookkeeping after call 1.
- Cover the claim step in the same diagnosis and fix: a `build,test` Task call that reaches build commits without `/flow` Step 2.8 having claimed the group (no `claims/issue-{n}.json` under this run's `runId`, no `bot:in-progress`) must fail loud before its first commit, never proceed — the record-976 run duplicated already-merged work because nothing checked. The disposition items #1832 filed for that run are moot (its worktree and branch are gone, #1100/#1484 closed, PR #1730 closed) and need no work.
- Close #1858, #1832, and #1810 as absorbed once this record's fix lands, naming which hypothesis held.
- (#1810) Have the Manifesto's `config.yml` write log the absolute path it wrote (`AUTO … — Manifesto: levers written to {absolute path}`), the way `record-pr`/`record-worktree` log their targets, so a shadow-path write and a later removal from the anchored directory can be told apart from the artifacts.
- (#1810) In `steps-and-gates.md`'s case 3, name `decisions.md`'s "Pipeline config snapshot" header as the preferred lever source, ahead of recomputing from the precedence chain (recomputation can silently differ from what call 1 ran under), and widen case 3's description to cover a completed first call whose `config.yml` is missing — not only an interrupted one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `build,test` → `review,polish,wrap-up` two-call dispatch handoff leaves the run directory populated with `config.yml`, `decisions.md`, and `run-state.json`, and the branch pushed with a draft PR open, by the time the first call's `test` step exits — verified by a regression test that simulates the two-call split and asserts the anchored run directory's contents after call 1.
2. A resumed run found with an empty or partially initialized run directory despite existing build commits takes `preflight.js`'s backfill path (case 3 semantics) and the adoption note names each backfill performed; a run it cannot recover surfaces a clear, actionable error instead of continuing.
3. Every conditional skip on the Manifesto write and the PR-early bootstrap paths writes a `SKIP` entry to `decisions.md`; the two runs' shapes (empty directory; `decisions.md` without a Manifesto entry) can no longer occur without a log line.
4. `tests/dispatch-flow-rundir-handoff.test.js` (or a sibling) covers the shadow-write hypothesis: a `config.yml` written under `<worktree>/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run}/` is detected and rejected or redirected.
5. A `build,test` call whose run has no claim under its own `runId` for every group member stops with an actionable error before any build commit — covered by the regression test in AC 1 (a fixture where the claim step is skipped must fail, not build).
6. `npm test` passes; #1858, #1832, and #1810 are closed with a comment naming this record and the confirmed cause.
7. The Manifesto's `config.yml` write logs the absolute path; case 3's prose names the `decisions.md` snapshot header as the preferred lever source and covers the completed-first-call shape (#1810).

## Technical Approach

Start from evidence, not the prior fixes: for record-703's branch, list `<worktree>/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/` on the branch's tree at its last commit and in any surviving worktree — a shadow directory there settles hypothesis (a) immediately. For record-1484, read its `events.jsonl` for the first call's `PostToolUse`/`SessionStart` events to see which run the hooks attributed writes to. Then read `flow/steps-and-gates.md` Step 2 adoption cases against `preflight.js`'s predicates and `flow/manifesto.md` Step 3's write, and `build/worktree-setup.md` Step 6's call into `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`, looking for the branch that returns early when the directory pre-exists. The fix should make the write paths resolve the anchored directory through `resolve-run-dir` (never a cwd-relative path) and log a `SKIP` on every early return. Keep the regression test in the fixture-repo style `tests/dispatch-flow-rundir-handoff.test.js` already uses.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` — adoption case classification; case 2/3 boundary when commits already exist
- `plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md` — Step 2 adoption cases and the "do not re-initialize" rule
- `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto.md` — Step 3 `config.yml` write; add the `SKIP` degrade-trace on every skip path
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` — push/open-draft-PR procedure invoked from `build/worktree-setup.md` Step 6; skip-path logging
- `plugin/skills/build/worktree-setup.md` — Step 4.5 `record-worktree` and Step 6 bootstrap call site
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` — the two-call context pack's `{minted-run-dir}` substitution and `record-worktree` instruction
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — `checkPipelineShadowGuard`: whether writes into a pre-existing worktree-local shadow are caught
- `tests/dispatch-flow-rundir-handoff.test.js` — regression test for the two-call split and the shadow-write case

## Gotchas

- Three closed records (#1013, #1129, #1145) already "fixed" this symptom; a fourth fix that does not first identify which path the earlier fixes missed will regress the same way. The diagnosis deliverable is not optional.
- `checkPipelineShadowGuard` flags only a *new* run directory created inside a worktree; a pre-existing shadow (from a pre-anchoring run, or a copy) is left alone by design — a write into it is silent.
- `preflight.js`'s case 1 rule "never re-initialize `config.yml`/`decisions.md`" is load-bearing for the second call; the case 2/3 change must not overwrite an interrupted first call's audit trail.
- Record-1484's run had `run-state.json` without `pr` — `record-worktree` ran but the PR-early bootstrap did not; that ordering narrows the search to Step 6's own guard, not adoption as a whole.
- The regression test needs a fixture with a real `origin` remote (bare repo) for the push/PR half; mock `gh` at the seam the existing handoff test already uses.

## Original request

Two-call dispatch handoff again left run dir empty (no config.yml/run-state.json/PR) despite build commits already present — recurrence of #1013/#1129/#1145

## Current State

Run `2026-09-04T095553-record-703` (dispatch bundle group for #703, `build,test` then `review,polish,wrap-up` two-call handoff) was resumed for its second call (`review,polish,wrap-up`) with:

- `git log` showing build had already completed and committed multiple times against the materialized spec (`698f19e51` materialize, through `0635a52db` "Record Task 0 empirical findings for #703"), including a real implementation, tests, and a written plan doc.
- The run directory (`$RUN_ROOT/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-04T095553-record-703/`) was **completely empty** — no `config.yml`, no `decisions.md`, no `run-state.json`, not even a `staged/` directory.
- The branch (`worktree-dispatch-record-703`) had never been pushed to `origin`, and no draft PR existed for it — despite `build/worktree-setup.md` Step 6's PR-early bootstrap being documented as running "immediately after the materialize commit, before Spec Step 2."

This reproduces the same failure shape as #1013 / #1129 / #1145 (all closed) — a split `build,test` → `review,polish,wrap-up` dispatch handoff loses the run directory's `config.yml`/`run-state.json` and the PR-early lifecycle bootstrap, even though those issues were closed as fixed. Either the fix didn't cover this exact code path, or a regression reintroduced the gap.

**Downstream cost this run:** the code-simplifier subagent dispatched from `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 5 was BLOCKED outright by the `worktree-always`/bookkeeping-stamps PreToolUse gate, which requires a draft PR to exist before any Edit/Write in a `pr-first` worktree — because no PR had ever been opened. Origin: wrap-up leftover from #2028

## Current State

`tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js:186,204` (`CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS env override raises the
budget…` and `an explicit opts.timeoutMs still wins…`) deliberately race a `timeoutMs: 1`
override against a real `git rev-parse` subprocess and assert the timeout branch fires. During
#2028's wrap-up: full `npm test` — 1 fail (this file). Three isolated re-runs (`node --test
tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js`) — 2 failed (same assertion, `null` where `'timeout'` was
expected — the subprocess completed inside 1ms under a lightly-loaded run), 1 passed clean
(18/18). No change in #2028's own diff (bookkeeping-only) touches `runGit`/`runGitAsync` or any
caller in `hooks.js`. Same machine-load-timing-race shape as the sibling flaky-allowlist
proposal for `tests/reconcile.test.js` (#2499).

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-exec.js`'s own header comment (lines 7-12) names the fix technique
directly: the module deliberately calls `cp.execFileSync(...)` via property access rather than a
destructured import specifically so "a test's `t.mock.method(cp, 'execFileSync', ...)`" can
intercept it — this module was built anticipating exactly this kind of mock-injection test need,
but the two flaky tests don't use it; they race a real subprocess against wall-clock time
instead. `classify()` (`git-exec.js:77-87`) determines `FAILURE.TIMEOUT` from `err.code ===
'ETIMEDOUT' || err.killed === true || err.signal === 'SIGTERM'` — a synthetic error carrying any
one of those is classified identically to a real timeout kill, so a mock can exercise the same
classification logic under test without spawning a real process or waiting on real time.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Rewrite both races (`tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js:186` and `:204`) to use
      `t.mock.method(cp, 'execFileSync', ...)` (the technique `git-exec.js`'s own header comment
      already names) throwing a synthetic error with `killed: true, signal: 'SIGTERM'` instead of
      racing a real `git rev-parse` subprocess against `timeoutMs: 1` — deterministic regardless
      of machine load, no wall-clock dependence at all.
- [ ] If a genuinely real-subprocess-timeout test still has independent value (e.g. an
      integration-style smoke test that `execFileSync`'s own timeout mechanism actually fires),
      keep at most one such test and move it out of the main suite's default fast path, or accept
      it as the allowlist fallback below — but the two tests this record targets should not stay
      wall-clock races once the mock-based rewrite lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Under contended machine load, neither test fails on timing alone — the mock-based rewrite makes
  both deterministic, not merely more tolerant.
- Both tests still correctly distinguish the two behaviors they exist to pin: the env-var budget
  override applies when `opts.timeoutMs` is absent, and an explicit `opts.timeoutMs` still wins
  over the env var when both are present.
- `npm test` passes, including 10+ consecutive isolated runs of `tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js`
  with no timing-related failure (verifying the race is actually eliminated, not just less
  likely).

## Technical Approach

For each of the two tests, replace the real `runGit(['rev-parse', ...], dir, { timeoutMs: 1 })`
call (or `runGitAsync`'s twin) with a `t.mock.method(cp, 'execFileSync', () => { const e = new
Error('mock timeout'); e.killed = true; e.signal = 'SIGTERM'; throw e; })` stub scoped to that
test (restored via the mock's own teardown or a `finally`, matching the existing
`CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` env-var save/restore pattern already in both tests). Call `runGit`
exactly as today; only the underlying subprocess call is intercepted, so the env-var-vs-opts
precedence logic under test runs unmodified. `runGitAsync`'s twin (line ~175, the earlier
`Promise.all` shape test) is a different test not targeted by this record — check whether it
shares the same race and needs the identical treatment as part of this fix, since it calls
`runGitAsync(..., { timeoutMs: 1 })` against a real subprocess too.

### Key Files

- `tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js:186-218` — the two tests to rewrite
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-exec.js:1-12` (header comment, the anticipated mock technique),
  `:77-87` (`classify()`, the logic under test, unmodified)
- `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` — only touched if the allowlist fallback is taken instead

## Gotchas

- Don't mock `execFileSync` so broadly that it also intercepts the *success* path other tests in
  this file rely on — scope the mock to only the two tests being rewritten, restored immediately
  after each.
- Same underlying flakiness family as #2499 (`tests/reconcile.test.js`) — both are wall-clock
  races against real subprocess/timer completion under load — but the fixes diverge: #2499's
  concurrency assertion has no real-subprocess mock point available and needs an overlap-based
  rewrite, while this record's tests are racing a subprocess that `git-exec.js` was already built
  to let a test intercept.

Surface: infra

Origin: wrap-up leftover from #2028
Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

`tests/reconcile.test.js:1491` (`reconcile(): FAST_CHECKS runs the preflight and the shared
fetch concurrently, not serially (#872)`) failed once in a full `npm test` run (8988 tests,
127s; elapsed 463ms vs. an expected ~200ms concurrency window), during #2028's wrap-up.
Isolated re-run (`node --test tests/reconcile.test.js`) passed cleanly, 103/103, the same test
completing in 323ms. No change in #2028's own diff (bookkeeping-only: a materialized spec file,
a plan, and a ledger) touches `reconcile()`, its preflight, or its shared-fetch path — this is a
timing-sensitive assertion racing against machine load from the full suite, not a regression.

The test asserts `elapsed < HEALTH_DELAY_MS * 2` (400ms) after `Promise.all`-dispatching a mocked
`ghHealthCheckAsync()` (artificially delayed 200ms) alongside the real `sharedFetchAsync()` call
(`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js:207-209`, a genuine local-fixture `git fetch` — not
artificially delayed). Widening the margin further (e.g. 3x/600ms) would reduce false failures
under load but also erodes the test's ability to actually catch a regression to serial
execution: a serial run only adds `sharedFetchAsync`'s own real (likely small) duration on top of
the 200ms mock delay, so a wide enough margin to absorb load jitter risks being wide enough to
also absorb an actual serial regression — the margin and the detection power trade off directly
against each other on a wall-clock assertion. `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` has no `flaky`
key today — the allowlist schema this record's second option proposes doesn't exist yet and would
be a new subsystem built for one test.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Either loosen the timing assertion (e.g. widen the window, or assert ordering/concurrency
      via a mechanism other than wall-clock elapsed time), or add `tests/reconcile.test.js` to
      `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json`'s `flaky.files` allowlist with a `maxRetries: 1` entry
      and a per-suite `retry` command template (`"retry": {"tests": "node --test {file}"}` —
      the project's only declared suite key is `tests`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Under contended machine load (a concurrent `npm test` run on the same host), this test no
  longer fails on timing alone — either the assertion tolerates load, or the allowlist entry
  retries it once and the retry passes.
- The test still fails if `FAST_CHECKS` regresses to serial dispatch of the preflight and the
  shared fetch (no loss of detection power as a side effect of the fix).

## Technical Approach

Recommended: replace the wall-clock margin with a deterministic overlap assertion, not a wider
threshold. Record each call's own start/end timestamp inside the test (wrap `ghHealthCheckAsync`
and `sharedFetchAsync` — or intercept via the same mock-injection points the test already uses
for `ghHealthCheckAsync`, adding an equivalent timing wrapper around `sharedFetchAsync` if one
isn't already injectable) and assert the two calls' `[start, end]` windows overlap (e.g.
`healthStart < fetchEnd && fetchStart < healthEnd`). Concurrent dispatch always overlaps; serial
dispatch never does, regardless of how fast or slow the machine is that run — this is immune to
load-induced jitter in a way no wall-clock threshold can be, without sacrificing the ability to
catch a genuine regression to serial execution.

Prefer this over both options the record's Deliverables originally proposed: widening the
existing margin trades detection power for stability (see Current State); the `flaky.files`
allowlist route requires designing and building a new `verify-scope.json` schema field and its
consuming retry logic for the sake of one flaky test, a disproportionate lift for this record's
actual scope. If the overlap-based rewrite proves impractical during implementation (e.g. the
current mock-injection points for `sharedFetchAsync` don't support timing instrumentation
cleanly), fall back to widening the margin as documented above, but only as a fallback — not the
default plan.

### Key Files

- `tests/reconcile.test.js:1491-1525` — the assertion to rewrite
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js:207-209` — the `Promise.all([ghHealthCheckAsync(),
  sharedFetchAsync(...)])` dispatch under test
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/shared-fetch.js` — `sharedFetchAsync`'s definition, for whatever
  mock-injection point an overlap rewrite needs
- `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` — only touched if the fallback (allowlist) path is taken

## Gotchas

- Don't just widen the multiplier as a quick fix without reading the Current State's tradeoff
  above — it silently weakens the regression this test exists to catch.
- This is a test-only change — no production code in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/` should need to
  change for either the recommended fix or the fallback.

Origin: filed by the docs-health curation row (`/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`, D1 restructural), during #2322's wrap-up.

## Current State

`docs/plugin-structure.md`'s `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/` inventory paragraph states: "Both destructive branch checks read it screen-then-confirm: archive-branches and prune-remote screen the in-scope set in one bulk call and re-read per-branch only to confirm a destructive provisional verdict."

This is no longer accurate for `archive-branches.js`. Since #2252 (and widened by #2322), a MERGED-screened or screen-null non-cherry-equivalent branch reaches the per-branch confirm even when its provisional verdict is a non-destructive `skip` — the confirm's own squash-provenance evidence, not the provisional verdict, decides whether the branch is actually destructive. Between cli-v3.6.0 and cli-v4.0.0, pbakaus/impeccable's CLI engine was rewritten from JavaScript (shipped inline in the npm package, under cli/engine/) to Rust (crates/ in the upstream repo), compiled to a per-platform binary. Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/bin/hooks.js`'s `archive-run` verb prints the result of `archiveRunDir(mainRoot, runDir)`. One reason gets a bespoke six-line recovery message, selected by `if (result.reason === 'audit-untracked')` and interpolating `result.untrackedAuditFiles`; every other refusal prints `claude-tweaks: archival refused — {reason}`. `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` produces fourteen distinct reason codes (`move-failed`, `readdir-failed`, `mkdir-failed`, `console-unresolved`, `console-never-rendered`, `tracked-entry`, `no-pr`, `no-branch`, `network-failure`, `ls-files-failed`, `gh-absent`, `close-write-failed`, `close-failed`, `audit-untracked`, plus `git-mv-failed`/`git-mv-failed-partial-revert`) as ad hoc `{ ok: false, reason, … }` literals, some with extra fields (`lastError`, `untrackedAuditFiles`) that only the dispatcher knows to read. The recovery knowledge for `audit-untracked` lives 400 lines away from the code that detects it, and a rename of the reason code in `archive-merged.js` would silently downgrade the message to the generic line — nothing pins the two together. `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` asserts the message text (`archival refused — audit-untracked`, `sync this checkout with origin`), so the text can move but not change.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `archive-merged.js` gains one refusal constructor, `refusal(reason, { hint = null, ...extra } = {})` → `{ ok: false, reason, hint, ...extra }`, and every `{ ok: false, reason: … }` literal in the file goes through it, so each result carries a `hint` key (string or `null`) beside its reason.
- [ ] The `audit-untracked` recovery text moves verbatim from `hooks.js` into that refusal's `hint`, built where `untrackedAuditFiles` is computed; `move-failed` and the two `git-mv-failed*` refusals set `hint` from `lastError` when present; the other codes start with `hint: null` (no invented prose).
- [ ] `hooks.js`'s `archive-run` branch drops the `reason === 'audit-untracked'` match and prints `claude-tweaks: archival refused — {reason}` followed, when `result.hint` is a non-empty string, by ` — {hint}`; the exit code and the `moved:` lines are unchanged.
- [ ] A conformance test that every `reason: '…'` literal in `archive-merged.js` sits inside a `refusal(` call (a source scan), and unit cases that `refusal` always yields a `hint` key and that the `audit-untracked` result's hint names its files.
- [ ] `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` passes unmodified (its regexes match the moved text); `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` cases that deep-equal a refusal object are updated only to include `hint: null` where they assert whole objects.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `hooks.js` contains no comparison against a specific `archive-merged.js` reason string; the `archive-run` branch reads only `ok`, `reason`, `hint`, and `movedEntries`.
2. `node bin/hooks.js archive-run` on the untracked-audit fixture prints the same `audit-untracked` sentence as today (the existing test's regexes are the proof); every other refusal prints its reason exactly as today, with a hint appended only where one was set.
3. Every refusal object `archiveRunDir` and its helpers return has a `hint` property; the source scan finds no bare `{ ok: false, reason:` literal outside `refusal`.
4. `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Co-locate the story with the detector, keep the dispatcher dumb: a `hint` field is the smallest contract change that lets the next non-obvious failure ship its recovery text without a new `if` in `hooks.js`, and a constructor is what makes "every refusal has the field" a source-scannable invariant rather than a convention. Hints stay `null` for the codes whose one-line reason already says what happened (`gh-absent`, `no-pr`); writing prose for all fourteen would be the speculative work the record warns against. The `console-*` and `network-failure` codes come from `decideArchive`'s pure skip path (`{ action: 'skip', reason }`), which is a different shape consumed inside the loop, not by `hooks.js` — leave it alone and say so in the constructor's comment.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `archiveRunDir`, `archiveOrphanedMint`, `revertWorkMoves`/`revertPlainMoves`, the `audit-untracked` branch (`untrackedAuditFiles`), every `ok: false` literal.
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — the `archive-run` verb's refusal printing.
- `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` — text pins (unchanged); `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — object-shape cases.

## Gotchas
- The `audit-untracked` sentence is asserted by regex in `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js`; move it character-for-character, including the `git pull, or reconcile's own mirror-ff` clause.
- `trackArchiveResult` in the same file consumes `result.reason` and `result.lastError` for residue tracking; adding `hint` must not change what it reads, and `lastError` stays as its own field rather than being folded into `hint`.
- #1732 (classifier) and #1733 (loop extraction) touch the same file; this record touches only the refusal literals and can land before or after either, but never in parallel with them.
- Do not print hints for `dryRun` skips: `archiveMerged`'s `skipped` entries are a different consumer and the reconcile report renders them itself.

## Original request

`plugin/bin/hooks.js` has a single hardcoded `if (result.reason === 'audit-untracked')` branch that prints a bespoke multi-line recovery message, while `archive-merged.js`'s ~15 other reason codes (`mkdir-failed`, `git-mv-failed`, `ls-files-failed`, `tracked-entry`, `commit-failed`, ...) all fall through to a generic one-line message. The rich, actionable recovery text lives in the CLI dispatcher rather than co-located with the code that understands the failure, and nothing keeps a renamed/removed reason code in `archive-merged.js` in sync with this dispatcher-side string match.


Defer-reason: genuinely-larger — touches the reason-code contract across archive-merged.js's ~15 failure paths and its hooks.js dispatcher, not a localized change; found by the pre-v6.117.0 whole-branch review.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` parks a group's PR as `pending-review` when it has no `auto:merge` grant, or `assess-agent-autonomy`'s `merge-check` mode declines auto-merge (`dispatch/SKILL.md`'s Auto-merge gate, `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`). Under `integration-model: pr-first`, this PR is already public and current (`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` opened it at run start; every phase exit since has pushed to it) — `dispatch/reporting.md`'s own note on parking states the branch "never waited on parking to become public in the first place."

Two distinct resumption paths already exist for a **still-active dispatch session**: `dispatch/reporting.md`'s "resuming a parked run" (re-invoking the same session to answer its Review Console) and `resume-confirmation.md`'s confirm-before-resume gate. Neither applies to this record's actual gap: a `pending-review` PR that a human reviews and approves **directly on GitHub**, days or weeks after the dispatching session ended, with no live session left to resume. For that case, nothing in the plugin re-verifies the PR's CI is still green (rather than stale from an earlier infrastructure blip), converts a still-draft PR to ready, flags a PR that quietly went from clean to conflicting while parked, or performs the merge (and any deploy) once approval is confirmed — all of it currently done by hand with raw `gh`/`git` commands. `/tidy`'s Step 4.8 (`_shared/github-pr-scan.md`'s `repo-wide` scope) already **surfaces** exactly this class of PR as a `STAGED` finding (report-only, per its documented "never edits" posture) — but surfacing is not closing out.

## Deliverables

- A close-out capability for an approved `pending-review` PR, covering at minimum: (1) re-verify CI is currently green (not a stale prior result), (2) convert a still-draft PR to ready-for-review/merge, (3) detect and flag a PR that has gone from mergeable to conflicting since it was parked, (4) merge on confirmed approval, with an optional deploy step where the project has one.
- A confirmation gate before merge — mirroring `resume-confirmation.md`'s existing "confirm before resuming" posture (unconditional at every `autonomy` tier, including `unattended`) — since this closes out a PR with no live session's Review Console already having asked the merge question.
- Decide where this capability lives: extending `/tidy`'s Step 4.8 `pending-review` surfacing from report-only into an actionable close-out lane (it already does the discovery work), or a new bare-drain-style mode on `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` that re-adopts a `pending-review` group's claim and runs the close-out sequence headlessly. Either integration point reuses existing machinery (`assess-agent-autonomy`'s `merge-check`, `_shared/pr-first-merge.md`'s merge mechanics, the claims protocol for re-adoption) rather than inventing a parallel one — this decision is left to the build step, not prescribed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a `pending-review` PR whose CI last ran before an infrastructure outage, the close-out re-runs or re-checks CI before treating it as green.
- [ ] Given a still-draft `pending-review` PR with human approval, the close-out converts it to ready before merging.
- [ ] Given a `pending-review` PR that has gone from clean to conflicting while parked, the close-out flags it rather than attempting a merge.
- [ ] Given a clean, approved, CI-green `pending-review` PR, the close-out merges it (and runs any project deploy step) only after an explicit confirmation gate — never silently, at any `autonomy` tier.
- [ ] The chosen integration point (extended `/tidy` Step 4.8, or a new `/dispatch` mode) is documented in `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s command reference and, if a new mode, added to `docs/skill-graph.md`'s edges per CLAUDE.md's cross-reference rule.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Reuse existing machinery rather than building parallel logic: `assess-agent-autonomy`'s `merge-check` mode for the mergeability/CI judgment, `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` for the actual `gh pr merge` mechanics, and the issue-claims protocol (`_shared/issue-claims.md`) to re-adopt a `pending-review` group's original claim (still held, since parking never releases it) rather than starting a fresh one. `resume-confirmation.md`'s existing `AskUserQuestion` shape and Recommended-derivation rule are the direct model for this record's own confirmation gate — read that file before designing a new one, since the two must never disagree on the same PR's state if a human could reach either path for the same PR. Start the "where does this live" decision (see Deliverables) by reading `/tidy`'s Step 4.8 surfacing logic (`_shared/github-pr-scan.md`) and `dispatch/reporting.md`'s parking/resumption sections side by side.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/reporting.md` — `pending-review` parking semantics, read-only reference
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/resume-confirmation.md` — the confirmation-gate model to follow

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js`
— all three confirmed still true at this shaping pass:

- **Read-back race** (~line 400): post-write verification (#2073) re-reads immediately with no
  retry/backoff (`if (!verifyClaimLanded(deps, repoSlug, issue, opts.runId, knownTip))`). On the
  contents-API transport `knownTip` is `null`, so the read-back hits GitHub's
  eventually-consistent contents API and can legitimately return the pre-write blob — a spurious
  exit 5 on a claim that actually landed. The file's own header already warns against
  eventually-consistent GitHub reads elsewhere.
- **Claim leak on abort** (~line 227, confirmed): `abort()` releases only `claimedThisRun`
  (`releaseClaimedThisRun(deps, repoSlug, opts.runId, claimedThisRun)`). `stopOrSkip(issue,
  'unverified', 'unverified', 5, {})` runs (confirmed, ~line 401) *before* the target is pushed
  onto `claimedThisRun` (the `claimedThisRun.push(issue)` call is one line after the verification
  check), so a target whose claim genuinely landed (just couldn't be verified back) leaks until
  TTL expiry with no `bot:in-progress` marker making it visible.
- **Stale doc comment** (~line 225, confirmed): `abort()`'s comment still enumerates only exit
  codes 3 and 4 ("`exitCode` is 3 for a `contested`/`inFlight` envelope, 4 for a `transient`
  one") — exit 5 (`unverified`) was added without updating it.

- Add a bounded retry/backoff to the post-write read-back verification when `knownTip` is `null`,
  before declaring exit 5.
- Release (or otherwise make visible) the `unverified` target's claim on abort, not just
  `claimedThisRun`.
- Update `abort()`'s doc comment to include exit 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A simulated eventually-consistent stale read on the contents-API path no longer produces a
  spurious exit 5 within the retry window.
- An aborted run with an `unverified` target leaves that claim in a state a later run can
  detect/reclaim before TTL, not silently leaked.
- `abort()`'s doc comment lists exit codes 3, 4, and 5.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

For the read-back race: wrap the `verifyClaimLanded` call (~line 400) in a small bounded
retry loop (a few attempts with a short backoff) specifically for the `knownTip === null` case —

window is exhausted. For the claim leak: capture the `unverified` issue's claim state (the

genuinely-landed-but-unverified claim doesn't sit invisible until TTL; releasing it (so a later
run can pick it up cleanly) is the safer default over leaving it silently held. Update the
`abort()` doc comment in the same change.

  leak fix (~line 227, `abort()` and the `unverified` stop path), and the doc comment update

  correctness gain.

  produced — verify the release targets the same claim identity (`repoSlug`, `issue`, `opts.runId`)

## Current State

Origin: #1033 review — Step 3 Security lens (2 independent reproduction-pair agents both
independently flagged the same substance from different angles; direct-verification confirmed).
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger.

#1033 (`plugin/bin/lib/declined-learning/store.js`) added an optional `subject` field to
declined-learning entries, carrying free-form, agent-authored summary text (`draft.fingerprintBasis.summary`
for `/feedback`, an insight's own `description` for `/wrap-up` reflect) alongside the existing
opaque fingerprint hash. Two independent Security-lens review agents on #1033 flagged the same
underlying issue from different angles:

- `plugin/skills/feedback/session-evaluation.md`'s `dismissedSubjects` (sourced from `listDeclined`
  in `store.js`) is rendered verbatim into a future `/feedback` judge-dispatch prompt via
  `plugin/bin/lib/transcript-judge/watermark.js`'s `formatOffsetClause` —
  `plugin/skills/_shared/transcript-judge.md` requires it be quoted "verbatim" — with no escaping,
  length cap, or sanitization (`dismissedSubjects.join('; ')` spliced directly into the
  offset-clause template string, `watermark.js` line ~104).
- `plugin/skills/reflect/full-mode.md`'s Don't-capture step (line ~218) similarly calls
  `recordDecline(fingerprint, { reason, source: 'wrap-up', subject: description })`, storing a
  reflect insight's own `description` text as `subject` with no validation, later scanned by a
  future run's agent judgment.

The content in `subject` is agent-authored (a summary the agent itself wrote after reading session
transcript content — files, web fetches, tool output), not raw user input, so this is an *indirect*
channel: crafted content reaching a session transcript could in principle influence what an agent
writes into a `fingerprintBasis.summary`/insight `description`, which later gets stored and
recirculated as literal instruction-shaped text into a future privileged judge dispatch. This is
the same general "agent-authored text recirculates into a future prompt" pattern already pervasive
across this plugin (ledger entries, `decisions.md` lines, staged proposals are all agent-authored
prose later re-rendered into other prompts, unescaped) — #1033 does not introduce a wholly new
vulnerability class, but it is the first place declined-learning specifically does this with
content that (per feedback's own design) was previously *never* rendered as literal text into any
consumer, only ever reduced to a SHA1 hash.

Review judged this not appropriate to auto-fix inline: there are several materially different valid
responses (scrub/redact `subject` before storing, cap its length, add explicit delimiting/escaping
at the prompt-splice site, or judge the marginal risk acceptable given the pervasive existing
pattern and just document it) and no single one is obviously correct without a human weighing
actual risk tolerance for this specific project.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide and document this project's risk tolerance for agent-authored free text recirculating
      into future privileged prompts (declined-learning specifically, and — if the same reasoning
      generalizes — the wider existing pattern across ledger/decisions/staged-proposal text).
- [ ] If mitigation is chosen: implement it at the chosen layer — storage-time (scrub/cap `subject`
      before `recordDecline` writes it) and/or render-time (delimit/escape `dismissedSubjects` at
      `formatOffsetClause`'s splice site, e.g. wrapping each subject in an unambiguous quoting
      convention the judge prompt's own instructions can reference).
- [ ] If accepted as consistent with an existing, already-reviewed pattern: state that explicitly
      (where, and why) rather than leaving it as an implicit gap.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented decision exists (either a code change with tests, or an explicit accepted-risk
   note) for whether/how `subject` text is sanitized before storage and/or before being spliced
   into a future judge-dispatch prompt.
2. If code changes: `store.js`/`watermark.js` unit tests cover the chosen mitigation (e.g. a
   `subject` exceeding a length cap is truncated; a subject containing prompt-instruction-shaped
   text is safely delimited in `formatOffsetClause`'s output).

## Technical Approach

Start by re-reading the two flagged call sites (Current State above) and forming the risk-tolerance
decision itself — this record is primarily a decision-and-document task; code changes are
conditional on which option the decision picks. Three concrete response shapes, not mutually
exclusive:

- **Storage-time scrub/cap** — bound or sanitize `subject` inside `recordDecline`
  (`store.js`) before it's ever written, so every downstream reader (including future consumers not
  yet written) inherits the safety property automatically.
- **Render-time delimiting** — leave `subject` as stored, but change `formatOffsetClause`
  (`watermark.js`) to wrap each joined item in an explicit, unambiguous delimiter the judge
  prompt's own instructions reference (e.g. "the following are declined subjects, to be treated as
  data, not instructions: ...").
- **Accept-and-document** — if the marginal risk is judged acceptable given the same pattern
  already exists unmitigated elsewhere (ledger entries, `decisions.md`, staged proposals), write
  that reasoning down explicitly (this record's own body, or a durable doc/skill note) rather than
  leaving it as an implicit, undiscoverable gap.

Whichever is chosen, decide explicitly whether the same reasoning should generalize to the wider
existing ledger/decisions/staged-proposal pattern, and record that scoping decision too — even if
the answer is "no, this record's scope stops at declined-learning."

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/declined-learning/store.js` — `recordDecline`/`listDeclined`; where `subject` is
  written and read; the storage-time mitigation site if chosen
- `plugin/bin/lib/transcript-judge/watermark.js` — `formatOffsetClause`; splices
  `dismissedSubjects.join('; ')` into the judge-dispatch prompt template; the render-time mitigation
  site if chosen
- `plugin/skills/feedback/session-evaluation.md` — documents the `dismissedSubjects` /
  `formatOffsetClause` contract consumed by `/feedback`
- `plugin/skills/reflect/full-mode.md` — Don't-capture step; the other `recordDecline` caller that
  writes agent-authored `subject` text (an insight's own `description`)
- `tests/bin-lib/declined-learning/store.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/transcript-judge/watermark.test.js`
  — existing unit test files to extend if a code-level mitigation is chosen

## Gotchas

- `subject` is agent-authored (derived from session transcript content), not raw user input — the
  channel is indirect, so any mitigation should be judged against that lower likelihood, not treated
  as a direct-user-input injection risk.
- This is not a novel vulnerability class for this plugin — ledger entries, `decisions.md` lines,
  and staged proposals already recirculate agent-authored prose into other prompts unescaped. A
  decision to leave `subject` unmitigated is only defensible if that parallel is stated explicitly,
  not assumed.
- Prior to #1033, declined-learning content was only ever reduced to a SHA1 hash before reaching any
  consumer — `subject` is the first time literal text from this store reaches a rendered prompt, so
  "we already accept this risk elsewhere" needs to be checked against this specific store, not
  inferred from the wider pattern without looking.

Origin: wrap-up for #2428

## Current State

`bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `acceptance-labeling` check (registered around line 467)
unconditionally requires a resolved issue to carry `demo:pending` once it has a resolvable
carrier commit — `if (!labels.some((l) => l.name === 'demo:pending')) { failing.push(...'missing
demo:pending label'); }` — with no awareness of `verification-brief.md`'s Oversight-floor gate
(`#367`, `exceedsOversightFloor` in `bin/lib/issues/oversight-floor.js`). That gate deliberately
skips Steps 1-4 (no `demo:pending` bootstrap at all) whenever a record's `risk:*`/`size:*` facets
don't clear the project's `risk-floor`/`size-floor` policy — a documented, intentional "not
required" outcome, not a defect (`verification-brief.md`'s Oversight-floor gate section: "The
record closes with no `demo:*` label and no ceremony... It stays demoable later on request").

Reproduced during `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s Phase 4 verify step for #2428 (`risk:medium`,
`size:medium` against a project's `risk-floor: high`/`size-floor: high` — `exceedsOversightFloor`
correctly returned `{exceeds: false}`, Steps 1-4 correctly skipped, no `demo:pending` applied).
The `acceptance-labeling` check then reported `fail — #2428: missing demo:pending label`,
forcing wrap-up to exit code 3 (`On exit code 3, do NOT emit the closure line: surface BLOCKED`)
for a record that did nothing wrong.

## Deliverables

- Give `acceptance-labeling` a way to recognize a legitimate Oversight-floor skip and render
  `skip (below oversight floor -- demo:pending not required)` instead of `fail` for that case,
  without weakening the check for a record that genuinely should carry the label but doesn't.
- Likely shape: re-run (or read a cached result of) `exceedsOversightFloor` against the same
  `risk-floor`/`size-floor` policy values `verification-brief.md` used, keyed off the resolved
  issue's own `risk:*`/`size:*` facets — mirroring the same computation, not inventing a new
  signal. Consider whether this belongs in `engine-verify.js` directly or as a new
  `verify-expectations.json` field the Oversight-floor gate writes at skip time (parallel to how

## Current State
`checkWindowsLongpaths` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js` (around line 524-530, landed via #1785/#2432) runs `runGit(['config', '--get', 'core.longpaths'])` and treats any non-`'true'` stdout as "core.longpaths is not enabled" — including when `result.failure` is `'timeout'`, `'spawn'`, or `'no-git'` (the check never actually ran). It then unconditionally calls `logWindowsLongpathsEvent(ctx, { result: 'unset', value: result.stdout })` and surfaces the same warning message for both cases.

The sibling function 20 lines below, `checkWorktreeStaleness`, already draws this exact distinction correctly: it logs `result: 'check-failed'` and skips the message when `fetch.failure`/`revList.failure` is set, rather than asserting a fact it doesn't know. This file's own header comment (lines 14-18) states the indeterminate/definitive distinction matters "only where a gate acts on the answer" — this is exactly such a site.

Found by two independent reproduction-pair agents during the whole-branch pre-release review after v6.124.0 (base 05d7d6cc5..75f71e366), confirmed severity: medium.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `checkWindowsLongpaths` distinguishes a real `runGit` failure (`result.failure` set) from a definitive git-config answer, matching `checkWorktreeStaleness`'s existing `'check-failed'` convention
- [ ] On a real failure, skip the "core.longpaths is not enabled" warning (the check didn't run, so the fact is unknown) and log a distinct result value (e.g. `'check-failed'`) rather than `'unset'`
- [ ] Add test coverage for the forced timeout/spawn/no-git branches (currently only success and real-git-config-unset are covered — `tests/hooks-post-tool-use-worktree-staleness.test.js`)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A forced `runGit` failure (timeout/spawn/no-git) on the `core.longpaths` check never produces the "not enabled" warning and never logs `result: 'unset'`
2. `events.jsonl` can distinguish "checked, found unset" from "check didn't run" for this event, same as it already can for worktree-staleness events
3. New tests exercise the failure branches and would fail against the current code

## Technical Approach

In `checkWindowsLongpaths` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js:524-530`), split the current
single `if (!result.failure && result.stdout === 'true')` branch into two checks, mirroring
`checkWorktreeStaleness`'s existing shape (same file, line 571):

1. `if (result.failure) { logWindowsLongpathsEvent(ctx, { worktree: worktreePath, result: 'check-failed', reason: result.failure }); return null; }` — a real check failure never asserts "not enabled" and never returns the warning `systemMessage`.
2. The existing `result.stdout === 'true'` → `'enabled'` branch is unchanged.
3. Everything else (a clean, non-failing `--get` that returned non-`'true'` stdout, including empty stdout for a genuinely unset key) keeps today's `result: 'unset'` logging and warning.

No change to `checkWorktreeStaleness` itself — it's the reference pattern, not part of this fix.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js` — `checkWindowsLongpaths` (~line 513-544, the fix),
  `checkWorktreeStaleness` (~line 546, the reference pattern already correct)
- `tests/hooks-post-tool-use-worktree-staleness.test.js` — existing win32/longpaths coverage at
  line 231 (unset) and 240 (already-true); add a forced-failure case mirroring line 171's
  `checkWorktreeStaleness` fetch-failure test

## Gotchas

- Don't change the message text or the `'enabled'`/`'unset'` result values for the two paths that
  already work correctly (real true, real non-true) — only the previously-uncovered failure path
  changes behavior.
- The fix is a direct structural mirror of code already in the same file 20 lines away — no new
  pattern to invent, just apply the existing one.

## Current State

Ten call sites across `plugin/bin/` resolve an explicit `--repo` value by unconditionally
wrapping it as `` parseRepo(`github.com/${opts.repo}`) `` before parsing — so a caller-supplied
`--repo` can never target a non-github.com host, even after #2240 widened `parseRepo` itself to
return a `host` field. Only the git-remote fallback path (`parseRepo(remote)`, when `--repo` is
omitted) benefits from #2240's widening.

Confirmed live in the current tree:

- `plugin/bin/fetch-sub-issues.js:92`
- `plugin/bin/release-claim.js:138`
- `plugin/bin/file-feedback.js:112`
- `plugin/bin/apply-refine-labels.js:174`
- `plugin/bin/link-records.js:77`
- `plugin/bin/repair-claim.js:99`
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js:327`
- `plugin/bin/lib/compose-subject.js:179`
- `plugin/bin/preflight-records.js:115`
- `plugin/bin/backlog-grant-gate.js:148`

This is a distinct, still-live bug from #2443 (closed already-shipped, 2026-09-16): #2443 was
about `bin/lib/**` modules discarding a host that had already reached them; this record is about
the wrap that decides what `host` reaches them from `--repo` in the first place.

`plugin/bin/lib/number-list-cli.js:96-97` already carries the fix, landed as a review finding on
#2425: `parseRepo(opts.repo.split('/').length >= 3 ? opts.repo : \`github.com/${opts.repo}\`)` — a
3-segment `--repo` value (`host/owner/repo`, `repoSlug()`'s own GHE output shape) is passed through
unwrapped; a 2-segment `owner/repo` value still gets the `github.com/` prefix, unchanged. Its
regression tests (`tests/bin-lib/number-list-cli.test.js:166` and `:177`) are the reference
fixture shape for this record's own test coverage. `number-list-cli.js` is the shared scaffold
behind `resolve-blockers.js`/`resolve-linked-prs.js` only — the ten call sites above each hand-roll
their own `parseRepo` wrap independently and never picked up #2425's fix.

## Deliverables

- Apply `number-list-cli.js`'s exact segment-count check (`opts.repo.split('/').length >= 3 ?
  opts.repo : \`github.com/${opts.repo}\``) to each of the ten call sites listed above, replacing
  their unconditional `github.com/` wrap.
- Add one regression test per call site's existing test file, mirroring
  `tests/bin-lib/number-list-cli.test.js`'s two `#2425 review fix` cases: a host-qualified
  `--repo host/owner/repo` resolves to that host, and a bare `--repo owner/repo` still resolves to
  `github.com` unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the ten named call sites' `--repo` flag accepts a host-qualified `host/owner/repo` value
  and resolves `repoSpec.host` to that host, not `github.com`.
- Each of the ten named call sites' `--repo` flag still resolves a bare `owner/repo` value to
  `host: "github.com"` — no regression on the existing, far more common case.
- Every git-remote fallback path (`--repo` omitted) is unchanged — this record touches only the
  explicit-`--repo` wrap.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Replace the unconditional `` `github.com/${opts.repo}` `` (or `o.repo` — two of the ten sites use
that param name) template literal at each of the ten cited line numbers with
`number-list-cli.js:96`'s conditional: pass `opts.repo` through unwrapped when it already has 3+
